[CRITICAL] [CORRECTNESS] Broken contract in find_user (app/users.py)
- Issue: The change from `raise UserNotFound(user_id)` to `return None` breaks the function's contract. Callers shown in the reference context (`app/api.py`, `app/mailer.py`) expect the exception and do not guard against `None`. `api.py` will crash with `AttributeError` on `user.email` instead of returning 404; `mailer.py` will crash with `AttributeError` on `user.email`/`user.name` instead of propagating the missing-user error.
- Fix: Revert `app/users.py` to `raise UserNotFound(user_id)`, or update both callers to check `if user is None: ...` before attribute access.

[CRITICAL] LOGIC find_user returns None (at find_user)
- Issue: find_user returns None when the user is not found, breaking callers that expect either a User object or a UserNotFound exception. get_profile will attempt to access user.email and user.name on None, raising AttributeError, and send_welcome_email will similarly crash, while the API loses its 404 error handling.
- Fix: Restore the original behavior by raising UserNotFound(user_id) when row is None.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC get_profile fails to handle None return from find_user (at app/api.py:3-6)
  - Issue: The change to find_user returning None instead of raising UserNotFound breaks get_profile's exception handling. When user is not found, user becomes None, then user.email raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'email'. The try/except UserNotFound block never catches anything and the function crashes instead of returning 404.
  - Fix: Replace try/except with None check: `user = find_user(user_id); if user is None: return {"error": "not found"}, 404`

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC send_welcome_email crashes on None return from find_user (at app/mailer.py:3-8)
  - Issue: send_welcome_email directly accesses user.email and user.name without checking if find_user returned None. When user doesn't exist, user is None and accessing user.email raises AttributeError, crashing the function instead of handling the missing user gracefully.
  - Fix: Add None check: `user = find_user(user_id); if user is None: return` or raise an appropriate exception

* [WARNING] STRUCTURE UserNotFound exception class becomes dead code (at app/users.py:11)
  - Issue: The UserNotFound exception class is no longer raised by find_user, making it dead code. Any other code catching UserNotFound will silently fail to catch anything. This creates maintenance burden and potential for confusion.
  - Fix: Either remove the UserNotFound class entirely, or update all callers to use a different error handling pattern

* [WARNING] ERROR_HANDLING Inconsistent error handling across callers (at app/api.py, app/mailer.py)
  - Issue: The refactored find_user now returns None, but callers have different expectations - get_profile expects an exception to return HTTP 404, while send_welcome_email has no error handling at all. This inconsistency will cause some callers to crash while others silently fail.
  - Fix: Standardize on one pattern - either all callers check for None, or all callers expect exceptions. Consider using Optional[User] type hint to make the contract explicit

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Missing users now return an undocumented value to exception-based callers (app/users.py: `find_user`)
  - Issue: Changing `find_user` to return `None` for a missing user breaks the established exception contract. In `app.api.get_profile`, an unknown `user_id` no longer reaches the `except UserNotFound` branch; it proceeds to `user.email` and raises `AttributeError`, producing an unintended server error instead of a 404. `app.mailer.send_welcome_email` similarly dereferences `user.email` and `user.name`, so deleting a user or referencing a nonexistent ID crashes that flow.
  - Fix: Preserve the existing contract by keeping `raise UserNotFound(user_id)` and return `User(**row)` only when a row exists. If `None` is intentional, migrate every caller to check for it and define a return type that makes the nullable contract explicit.
